# UKIP 2017 Manifesto Summary

**"Britain Together"** represents UKIP's vision for a post-Brexit Britain, positioning the party as "the guard dogs of Brexit" and the nation's "insurance policy" against backsliding by other parties. Leader Paul Nuttall emphasises UKIP has consistently led on issues like EU withdrawal and points-based immigration, predicting others will eventually follow.

## Core Brexit Position

UKIP outlines six key Brexit tests: regaining legal sovereignty free from European courts; full migration control; restoring the 200-mile maritime exclusive economic zone; independent WTO membership and trade agreements; no divorce payment to the EU; and completion by end of 2019. The party criticises Article 50 as "a trap designed to obstruct countries from leaving" and argues Britain should have simply repealed the European Communities Act 1972. They accuse Theresa May of showing signs of capitulation and warn UKIP will hold her accountable.

Fishing features prominently—the CFP is called "an obscenity" that destroyed British fisheries. Brexit could make the industry worth £6.3 billion. UKIP would repeal the 1964 London Convention on Fishing and rebuild the domestic fleet.

## Economic Approach

UKIP proposes £35 billion in savings through cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, reforming the Barnett Formula, and ending EU contributions. No taxes would be raised. Key spending includes:

- £11 billion extra annually for NHS and social care
- Personal allowance raised to £13,500; 40% threshold to £55,000
- Inheritance tax threshold increased to £500,000 (transferable)
- Business rates cut 20% for small businesses
- VAT removed from energy bills, hot takeaways, and sanitary products
- TV licence abolished

The party pledges tough action on corporate tax avoidance, closing loopholes allowing multinationals to pay negligible tax.

## Immigration and Integration

UKIP proposes reducing net migration to zero over five years through an Australian-style points system, moratorium on unskilled immigration, and new visa categories. Integration is equally prioritised: they would ban the niqab and burqa in public, disband sharia councils, and enforce "one law for all." Zero tolerance is promised for FGM, forced marriage, and "honour" crimes—with proposals including mandatory screening for at-risk girls and prosecuting complicit parents. Schools suspected of Islamist influence would face immediate special measures.

## Public Services and Defence

NHS spending would increase substantially, with tuition fees scrapped for medical students (with service commitments) and the cap on medical school places raised. Defence spending would genuinely reach 2% of GDP plus £1 billion annually, reversing cuts that left Britain with its smallest army since Napoleonic times. Veterans would receive a dedicated administration, guaranteed jobs in security services, and protection from legal harassment.

## Social Policy

UKIP commits to maintaining pensioner benefits and the triple lock, reversing social care cuts, and abolishing the bedroom tax. Grammar schools would return to every town. Housing would be addressed through factory-built modular homes providing up to 100,000 affordable properties annually. Coastal enterprise zones would regenerate neglected seaside communities.

## Democratic Reform

Proportional representation would be introduced, the House of Lords abolished, and an English Parliament created. Local referenda would give communities binding power over major developments.

Throughout, UKIP frames itself as defenders of British values, ordinary working people, and those "left behind" by establishment politics—the only party willing to challenge political correctness and deliver the Brexit voters demanded.
